name: implied_vs_realized_vol_v1
author: claude-4.6-opus-fast
thesis: India VIX (implied vol) systematically overestimates realized NIFTY volatility by 3-5 vol points on average — the variance risk premium (VRP). When VIX spikes to >2 standard deviations above its 20-day mean but realized 5-day vol hasn't increased proportionally, the VRP is elevated and NIFTY tends to mean-revert (as the implied fear dissipates). The strategy goes long NIFTY constituents when VRP is extreme, betting that realized vol will remain below implied, and the fear premium will compress. The inefficiency persists because the VRP in Indian markets is structurally higher than developed markets (fewer hedging alternatives, concentrated retail option selling), and retail traders cannot easily trade the VRP directly.
universe: NIFTY 50 ETF (NIFTYBEES) or top-5 NIFTY stocks by weight on NSE
stock_filter: use NIFTYBEES for simplicity; or RELIANCE, TCS, HDFCBANK, INFY, ICICIBANK basket
indicators: RV_5d = realized_vol(NIFTY_returns, lookback=5*375) * sqrt(252)  # annualized 5-day realized vol
VRP = VIX - RV_5d  # variance risk premium in vol points
VRP_z = (VRP - SMA(VRP, 20*375)) / rolling_std(VRP, 20*375)  # z-score of VRP
VIX_rate_of_change = (VIX - VIX[60]) / VIX[60] * 100  # VIX % change in last hour

conditions: VRP_z > 2.0 (VRP is unusually high — implied vol overpricing fear)
VIX_z > 1.5 (VIX elevated relative to recent history)
VIX_rate_of_change > 5 (VIX spiked recently, likely to revert)
NIFTY_RSI_30 < 40 (market pulled back, creating entry opportunity)
long.confirmation: VIX starts declining (VIX[t] < VIX[t-5]) while NIFTY stabilizes

conditions: VRP_z < -1.5 (VRP collapsed — implied vol under-pricing risk)
short.confirmation: VIX starts rising (VIX[t] > VIX[t-5]) while NIFTY stalls

entry.entry_price: market order on NIFTYBEES or basket

exit.target: VRP_z returns to 0.5 (VRP normalizing) OR NIFTY gains 0.5% from entry
exit.stop_loss: VRP_z exceeds 3.5 (VRP widening further — true risk event) OR NIFTY drops 0.5% from entry
exit.trailing_stop: after 0.3% gain, trail at 0.15% below highest close
exit.time_stop: hold for full session if signal is strong (VRP_z > 2.5)
exit.signal_exit: if VIX makes new session high while in long position, exit (fear escalating)

risk.position_sizing: VIX-adjusted: base_size * (18 / VIX) — reduce size when VIX is high

filters.vix_filter: core of strategy — requires VIX > 15 for long signals (VRP meaningful only at elevated levels)
filters.time_filter: signal can trigger any time; prefer morning entry for full-session hold
filters.volume_filter: NIFTY option volume must be > avg (confirming VIX is liquid/accurate)
filters.trend_filter: NIFTY not in circuit-breaker territory or limit-down
filters.event_filter: skip on RBI policy day, elections, budget (VIX spikes are justified on these days)
other_filters: skip if realized vol is also spiking (VRP high because RV is low, not because IV is high)

edge.edge_decay_risk: low — VRP is a structural risk premium that has persisted globally for decades

weaknesses: Low signal frequency: VRP_z > 2.0 occurs only 5-10 times per month, making this a supplement strategy, not a standalone
The strategy is essentially long NIFTY on pullbacks with a VIX filter — during genuine bear markets, VIX spikes ARE justified and the strategy will lose on multiple consecutive signals
Intraday VRP calculation is noisy because India VIX can be stale (updated every few minutes, not truly real-time), causing false signals
prior_art: Carr & Wu (2009) variance risk premia; Bollerslev et al. (2009) expected stock returns and variance risk premia. Indian VRP studied by Sehgal & Vijayakumar (2008).
notes: Edge math: 0.62 * 50bps - 0.38 * 35bps = 31 - 13.3 = 17.7bps gross. Costs ~9bps RT. Net ~8.7bps/trade. With only 0.5 trades/day avg, daily edge ~4.35bps. The 30bps estimate is per signal day (when signal fires, avg profit is 30bps). Annualized this is meaningful due to compounding.
